# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Deaf monkey to report the bomb’s visible light so I can apply the manual. Since I cannot speak and the Blind monkey cannot see gestures, I am signaling the Deaf monkey to pay attention to the Blind monkey’s report and relay the observed light aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut. Also obtain and relay the Deaf monkey's readings for the display, light, and all three wires.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0. The light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are blue, red, green.

The display is 0, the light is red, and the wire positions are 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The manual says a red light requires cutting the red wire, so Blind must cut position 2. I am signaling Deaf with the number-two gesture so Deaf can relay the position to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light red; wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. Please apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.

The manual maps a red light to the red wire. Deaf’s reading places the red wire at position 2. I cannot speak to Blind directly, so I am signaling Deaf to relay that Blind should cut position 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual's instruction as plain words and give me the exact wire position, 1, 2, or 3. I cannot identify a gesture as a wire instruction.

The red light requires cutting the red wire, and the red wire is in position 2. I cannot speak, so I am signaling Deaf with the agreed two-finger gesture; Deaf can then state the instruction plainly to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed: wire 2 was correct and is now cut. I see yellow light, display 0, and remaining wires 1 blue and 3 green.

The bomb has changed. The new light is yellow, which requires cutting the blue wire. Of the remaining wires, position 1 is blue and position 3 is green, so Blind must cut position 1. I am signaling Deaf with the agreed one-finger gesture to relay position 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut; wire 1 is blue and wire 3 is green. Blind signaled three gestures: pointing directly at you, one raised index finger, then the I-love-you hand sign. You signaled one raised index finger.

The yellow light requires the blue wire, which is wire position 1. Blind’s requested code is one clear finger for position 1, so I am sending exactly that to Deaf for relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])

The red wire is already cut, and the current blue light requires cutting the green wire. The only remaining wire is position 3. I will signal Deaf with three index-pointing gestures so Deaf can relay position 3 to Blind.

```

```

Blind says to Mute: Please signal the manual's next instruction clearly for Deaf to relay. Wire 1 and wire 2 are already cut; wire 3 is the only remaining wire.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your three raised-index gestures, likely wire 3. Current state remains display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green.

The blue light requires cutting the green wire. Wire 3 is the only remaining wire and is green, so the correct instruction is to cut position 3. I am sending the agreed three-finger signal to Deaf for relay.

```
